clue.text: Produce information time and time again at the finish

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the next word is kept

blocks.note: gen is informal British slang for information
an era is a period of time
time once more, this time as its abbreviation T
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone churns out data over and over until the end.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN + ERA + T + E: time is used twice, first as a period, then as its one-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To generate something is to produce or create it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: A contemporary look

blocks.note: first meaning: someone of the same age or standing
second meaning: to gaze closely

explanation.surface: A modern-looking appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'contemporary' as an adjective describing a look; it is a noun for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as a noun for an equal of the same age group and as a verb meaning to stare or squint.

clue.text: Bad-tempered inspector keeps ring

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: Inspector Morse, the Oxford detective of novels and television
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A grumpy police inspector is holding on to a ring, perhaps as evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: MOR(O)SE. Inspector Morse is a famously grumpy fictional detective, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy, a close synonym of bad-tempered.

clue.text: Send two men to church

blocks.note: two short men's names, Des and Pat
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: An instruction to dispatch a pair of men off to church.
explanation.walkthrough: DES + PAT + CH. The clue doesn't say which two men; short names like these are common crossword fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To despatch (a variant spelling of dispatch) is to send off, as with a letter or messenger.

clue.text: Essential truth behind Shakespearean actor's words

blocks.note: one's behind is one's bottom; Bottom is also the weaver-actor in A Midsummer Night's Dream
an actor's words are lines

explanation.surface: Looking for the real meaning behind a Shakespearean actor's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essential truth behind' looks like one phrase; 'behind' is the start of the wordplay. Bottom is the amateur actor in A Midsummer Night's Dream, which makes 'Shakespearean actor' doubly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom line is an idiom for the fundamental point or final reckoning of a matter.

clue.text: Arrange to make a start

blocks.note: first meaning: to lay out or display in order
second meaning: to begin a journey or undertaking

explanation.surface: Making plans to get going.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to lay things out in order and to set off on a journey.

clue.text: Die when man's away

blocks.note: a man's name, Peter; the 's stands for 'is'
someone away from home is out

explanation.surface: Things fall apart when the man of the house is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'man's away' as 'Peter is out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To peter out is to dwindle and fade away, as an idiom for a thing dying gradually.

clue.text: Manoeuvre animal back with a jerk

indicators.note: going back means the letters of the animal run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a cat is an animal
a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: Steering an animal backwards with a sharp tug on the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' looks like part of the manoeuvre in the surface, but it defines its own short piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned move or manoeuvre to gain an advantage.

clue.text: Elicits girl's agreement to go in

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, so it is placed within

blocks.note: Eve is a girl's name; the possessive gives Eve's
OK signals agreement

explanation.surface: Someone draws out a girl's consent to enter.
explanation.walkthrough: EV(OK)ES: the possessive 's supplies the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to call forth or draw out a response, so it is a synonym of elicits.

clue.text: Listen to judge

blocks.note: first meaning: to take in sounds
second meaning: to try a case in court

explanation.surface: An instruction to pay attention to the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers perceiving sounds and also a court's formal trying of a case, as in hearing evidence.

clue.text: Foreign control of one's profession

blocks.note: first meaning: rule of a territory by an invading power
second meaning: one's job or trade

explanation.surface: Outsiders take charge of someone's line of work.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers military seizure of a country by another power and also a person's job.

clue.text: Bet it's good to walk slowly

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
to amble is to stroll at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: A wager that a slow stroll is beneficial.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamble is a risky wager, so it can stand for a bet.

clue.text: Bribe supporter to accept part

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: a backer is a supporter, especially a financial one
a hand is a part or share, as in having a hand in something

explanation.surface: Paying off a supporter so that they will take on a role.
explanation.walkthrough: BACK(HAND)ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhander is British slang for a bribe, money slipped secretly to someone.

clue.text: Not too late to go outside at close

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, wrapping it

blocks.note: arriving 'in time' means not being too late
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reminder that there is still time to step outside at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: IN TIM(AT)E. 'close' is the adjective, as in a close friend, not the verb or the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate describes a very close personal relationship or friend, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Tax cut

blocks.note: first meaning: a duty levied on goods
second meaning: to remove surgically

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a tax reduction; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Excise is a duty charged on certain goods, and also a verb meaning to cut out.

clue.text: Hot tea's ruined some china

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
Ming porcelain is a famous kind of Chinese china

explanation.surface: Spilt hot tea has damaged some valuable crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' looks like the cups; Ming is a dynasty whose porcelain is called Ming.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming means very hot, giving off vapour, as a hot drink does.

clue.text: Get depressed within an hour? See a psychiatrist!

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, so it is placed inside

blocks.note: to sink is to fall into low spirits
HR is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Advice that anyone feeling low within the hour should get professional help.
explanation.walkthrough: S(HR)INK. 'Shrink' is informal for a psychiatrist, short for headshrinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrink is slang for a psychiatrist, from the jocular term headshrinker.

clue.text: Rotten setback before finish

indicators.note: placed before means the second-named piece comes first in the answer

blocks.note: a knock is a setback or blow
food that has gone off is rotten

explanation.surface: A miserable blow just before the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten' reads as an adjective on 'setback', but it is its own piece and comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock off is an informal phrasal verb for stopping work at the end of the day.

clue.text: Swing with unusual ease between two points

indicators.note: unusual suggests out of the ordinary order, so the letters are rearranged
something between two things is set inside them

blocks.note: two compass points, south and west
taken as written

explanation.surface: Swinging with surprising ease from one point to another.
explanation.walkthrough: S + (EASE)* + W. Points in crosswords are usually compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Seesaw works as a verb meaning to swing or move back and forth, as a playground seesaw does.

clue.text: With money, it's simple to get expensive stuff

blocks.note: cash is money
mere means simple or nothing more than

explanation.surface: If you have cash, buying luxury goods is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' here means fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a costly fine wool fabric, so it is a pricey material.

clue.text: Excitement one found in west London

indicators.note: something found in a place is located inside it

blocks.note: Acton is a district of west London
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A thrill found in the western part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: ACT(I)ON. Acton is a suburb in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Action means lively activity and excitement, as in 'where the action is'.

clue.text: Agitation as some felt remorse

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are used, a run lifted from inside the words

blocks.note: the run spans the end of felt and the start of remorse

explanation.surface: Someone trembles with guilt as they feel regret.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a shaking or quiver, a physical sign of agitation.

clue.text: Twist in story is no good

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, so it is placed inside

blocks.note: a tale is a story
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A plot twist that ruins the story.
explanation.walkthrough: TA(NG)LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tangle is to twist together in a muddle, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Craftsman notes unusual mother and child

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
ma is an informal word for mother
a son is a child

explanation.surface: An artisan observes an odd mother-and-child pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' reads as a verb in the surface; it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason is a skilled worker who cuts and dresses stone, a kind of craftsman.

clue.text: Capture bear

blocks.note: first meaning: to seize
second meaning: to endure or put up with

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures catching a bear; 'bear' is the verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to seize and to tolerate, as in 'I can't take any more'.

clue.text: Instruct student to put up rent

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up means its letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: Telling a student to raise their rent.
explanation.walkthrough: L + LET read upwards gives the answer. L-plates mark learner drivers in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell someone to do something is to instruct or order them.

clue.text: Navy follows fashion to be up-to-date

indicators.note: one piece follows another, so it comes after it in the answer

blocks.note: a mode is a fashion or style
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The navy keeps up with trends to stay current.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means current or contemporary, a synonym for up-to-date.

clue.text: Animals with unrestricted energy

blocks.note: wild means untamed or unrestrained
life means vitality or energy

explanation.surface: Creatures bursting with boundless vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildlife is the collective term for animals living in their natural state.
